Aamir was a 54-year-old software engineer, a profession that had once brought him a sense of pride and accomplishment. He lived a solitary life, often finding comfort behind the screens of his computers, where he could lose himself in lines of code. However, a silence had fallen over him since the day he was assaulted. The traumatic event had occurred late one night when he was walking home from a friend's house. An encounter with a group of men escalated quickly, ending in a violent sexual assault that left him feeling shattered and profoundly changed. He had not only lost his sense of safety but also his belief in justice, as he felt that nothing had been done to hold his assailants accountable. The injustice of it all haunted him, reinforcing a deep-seated belief that he was somehow to blame for what had happened. He thought, "If I hadn’t walked that way, or if I had just been more careful, maybe it wouldn't have happened."

In the months that followed the assault, Aamir noticed a shift in himself. He found himself increasingly anxious, especially in situations where he could hear sirens. The dread that filled him at the sound of ambulances or police cars compelled him to avoid situations where he might hear them, as the fear of reliving that night felt insurmountable. The sound of ambulances or police cars filled him with dread, pulling him back to that night when he had felt utterly powerless. Each time the sirens blared, Aamir felt an overwhelming urge to retreat, believing that the only way to avoid reliving the trauma was to steer clear of any situation where he might hear them again. The fear of those sounds compelled him to avoid situations where he might hear them, as he had come to believe that staying away was the only way to protect himself from reliving that trauma. This overwhelming anxiety led Aamir to avoid places where he might hear sirens, as he believed that steering clear of those situations was the only way to keep himself from feeling that same fear again. In an effort to cope, Aamir began to avoid places that reminded him of the attack, steering clear of the area where it had occurred. He also found himself distancing from any public spaces where men congregated, convinced that being alone with men would trigger a similar experience. These choices compounded his triggers; every time he skirted around a group of men, he was reminded of his trauma, reinforcing his belief that the world was filled with threats he could not confront. Each time he encountered a group of men, the memories of that night surged back, compelling him to retreat further into isolation, as if the mere presence of others could ignite the fear he sought to escape. His avoidance extended to uniforms and weapons; he would feel a wave of panic wash over him whenever he encountered police officers or soldiers. Each encounter would send an alarm through his body, making him feel as if he were back in that moment of fear, heightening his sense of danger. This overwhelming sense of threat became a self-fulfilling prophecy, as it led him to withdraw further from public life, convinced that he was constantly under siege. The avoidance strategies he employed only heightened his anxiety, as he had never allowed himself to face the very reminders he sought to escape, leaving the dangers feeling as present as ever. With each act of avoidance, Aamir felt more convinced that he was incapable of handling the world outside his home, reinforcing the belief that he had become too fragile for life as he once knew it. With every act of avoidance, he felt an increased sense of danger; the more he distanced himself, the more convinced he became that he was surrounded by threats he could not face. As Aamir continued to navigate his life, he became increasingly aware of how these maladaptive strategies were shaping his world.
